checklist.notes: The target forms, short examples, and help request fit A1.2, but central directions use unsupported abstractions such as ‘finished action’, ‘past-time word’, ‘exact problem’, ‘extra vowel’, and ‘integrate’.
The present-versus-past contrast, irregular run/ran form, movement sense of run, syllable counts, and /lp/ final-cluster guidance are accurate at this introductory level.
The examples are understandable and broadly natural; the ‘I ran here’ setup is slightly under-motivated but remains possible in context.
Only expected overlap in the authorized movement-sense definition and target forms was found internally; no external originality conclusion is available.
Past simple, request-for-help, syllables, and movement run are introduced using only present simple and phonemes from the declared closure.
The text is English and every embedded ID belongs to the allowed or context-only sets in the reconstructed request.

methods: Manual comparison of lesson wording with the supplied authoritative request and project-authored teaching payload.
Exact contiguous-word overlap comparison across the ten supplied v3 lesson bodies.
Inspection of the accepted audit provenance/copyright scope without consulting external sources.
copyright_originality_check.scope_limitations: No suspicious unexplained copying was found within the supplied scope. Reuse of target forms, short pedagogical frames, and project-authored definitions/examples is expected. No external search was performed; this is not a plagiarism clearance or copyright guarantee.

findings.description: The lesson’s learner-facing explanations and checks depend on grammatical and phonological metalanguage that is not explained at A1.2. This affects the instructions for every major target, not merely optional enrichment.
findings.recommendation: Use short concrete commands and timelines, define ‘past’ and ‘extra sound’ in simple language, and provide Vietnamese scaffolding for unavoidable technical terms.

findings.description: ‘I ran here, but I cannot find Gate 2’ is grammatical but gives little situational reason for mentioning the running, making the model sound pedagogically assembled.
findings.recommendation: Supply a natural link, for example that the speaker ran to the station and arrived late, before asking for the gate.

limitations: Review used only the exact lesson, accepted audit, regenerated hash-matching authoritative request, and verified M5 development snapshot; generator reasoning and prior review records were excluded.
No audio was supplied; pronunciation judgments cover written instructions and IPA only, not realized speech or learner performance.
No external CEFR vocabulary profiler or corpus was used; CEFR findings are qualitative independent AI judgments about the learner-facing text.

Originality checking was limited to the supplied authoritative payload and the ten supplied v3 lessons; no Internet, external corpus, or plagiarism search was performed, so no external plagiarism or legal-clearance claim is made.
